name: South Carolina

sales.rateNote: Statewide 6% sales and use tax on goods and certain services: a 5% base tax (SC Code 12-36-910) plus an additional 1% imposed since June 1, 2007 (12-36-1110). Voter-approved county taxes come on top.

local.levies: counties (Local Option, Capital Projects, Transportation, School District, Education Capital Improvement, County Green Space, Catawba Tribal) and municipalities (Tourism Development, Myrtle Beach); most require voter approval
local.capNote: Each local tax is generally 1% (Transportation and Green Space taxes up to 1%); combined county rates listed by the SCDOR range from 6% to 9% in total.

groceries.note: Unprepared food eligible for SNAP is exempt from the 6% state tax only (SC Code 12-36-2120(75)); local sales taxes can still apply, though Capital Projects, Education Capital Improvement and some Transportation taxes exempt it.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable except during the August sales tax holiday.

otherRates.note: 5% sales tax plus 2% state accommodations tax; local governments can add up to 3% more.

otherRates.item: Max Tax items (boats, aircraft, certain light construction equipment)
otherRates.note: Taxed at 5% with a maximum of $500 per item; local sales taxes do not apply.

otherRates.item: casual excise tax on boat, motor and airplane titles
otherRates.note: 5% of fair market value when a title or registration is issued.

holidays2026.name: Sales tax holiday (back to school)
holidays2026.items: clothing, clothing accessories, footwear, school supplies, computers, printers and software, bed and bath linens; excludes jewelry, cosmetics, eyewear, watches, furniture, layaway and business purchases. No price cap.

sales.holidayNote: Dates derived from the statute (12:01 a.m. on the first Friday in August through midnight the following Sunday), which falls on August 7-9 in 2026.

useTax.note: Use tax is due on goods used in South Carolina when South Carolina sales tax has not been paid; local use taxes also apply.

facts.text: Groceries escape the 6% state tax but not necessarily local taxes: in counties with a Local Option tax, food remains taxed at the local rate.
Lexington County extended its School District tax on March 1, 2026; Williamsburg County added a Capital Projects tax on May 1, 2026, bringing its total rate to 8%.
The 1% Local Option Sales Tax is used to reduce property taxes in the counties that adopt it.
Max Tax: boats and airplanes pay 5% capped at $500 per item, and local taxes do not apply.
The August holiday has no price limit per item, unlike most other states' back-to-school holidays.
Calls to 900 and 976 telephone numbers are taxed at 11%.

property.levied: local (counties, municipalities, school districts and special districts); collected by the county treasurer

assessment.text: Taxable value = fair market value x assessment ratio. A legal residence (owner's domicile, up to 5 acres) is assessed at 4%; other property, such as second homes and rentals, at 6%. Counties reappraise every fifth year, and increases from reappraisal are capped at 15% over five years (Act 388) unless the property is sold.
assessment.capText: Taxable value = fair market value x assessment ratio. A legal residence (owner's domicile, up to 5 acres) is assessed at 4%; other property, such as second homes and rentals, at 6%. Counties reappraise every fifth year, and increases from reappraisal are capped at 15% over five years (Act 388) unless the property is sold.

homestead.name: Homestead Exemption
homestead.text: The first $50,000 of fair market value of the legal residence is exempt from county, municipal, school and special assessment taxes for residents aged 65+, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind. For tax year 2026, the state temporarily authorized an additional homestead exemption for certain recipients.
homestead.applyBy: Apply through the county auditor's office.

otherRelief.name: School operating millage exemption
otherRelief.text: Owner-occupied homes receiving the 4% legal residence ratio are 100% exempt from property taxes levied for school operations (not school debt).

otherRelief.name: Disabled veteran exemption
otherRelief.text: Veterans with a total and permanent service-connected disability are exempt on their home and up to five acres, provided it receives the 4% legal residence ratio.

dueDates.text: Property taxes are due between September 30 and January 15 following assessment; counties may offer installment plans.

facts.text: The 4% legal residence ratio must be applied for with the county assessor before the first penalty date; it is lost if the home is rented more than 72 days a year.
The 15% cap on reassessment increases resets when the property is sold (an 'assessable transfer of interest'), so buyers are taxed on the full current value.
Owner-occupied homes pay no school operating millage, which shifts that cost to second homes, rentals and businesses assessed at 6%.
The state reimburses counties and school districts for the homestead exemption through the Trust Fund for Tax Relief.
Reappraisal values are completed at the end of December of the fourth year and owners are notified of changes of $1,000 or more.

uncertain: The amount of the temporary additional homestead exemption for tax year 2026 is not stated on the SCDOR page.
Motor vehicles are subject to the Infrastructure Maintenance Fee (SCDMV), not sales tax; its rate and cap were not verified.
Whether local sales taxes are also suspended during the August holiday was not verified.
Holiday dates are computed from the statute; no 2026 SCDOR holiday page was found (URLs tried returned 404).
